_provenance.source: FAA d-TPP cycle 2610 instrument approach plates for KBOS (the PDFs listed in kbos-procedures.json)
_provenance.method: Glidepath angle / TCH and the missed approach climb altitudes were read from each plate render (profile view "GS 3.00 / TCH 51", MISSED APPROACH box) and cross-checked against the pdfjs-dist text layer ("GS 3.00 TCH 51" strings). The SA CAT I and CAT II-III plates repeat the glideslope and missed approach of the standard ILS. RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 has no vertical guidance: its 2.91 deg / TCH 45 is a visual descent angle (VDA). HUMAN TRANSCRIPTION - verify against the PDFs before any real use.
_provenance.terms: TCH = threshold crossing height above the runway threshold of the plate's glidepath (GS = ILS glideslope, GP = RNAV glidepath, VDA = visual descent angle of a non-precision approach). It is NOT the VGSI TCH printed in the "(VGSI Angle x/TCH y)" note (KBOS: 67, 71, 71, 71, 68 for 4R, 15R, 22L, 27, 33L), which belongs to the visual glide slope indicator (NASR threshold_crossing_height_ft in the facility file).
